title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All directors, executives, employees, contractors, consultants and advisors of the Company and its subsidiaries. Bound by the insider trading prohibition and the discouragement of short-term trading at all times.

tiers.name: Directors and executives
tiers.description: A director or executive as determined by the Board. Must not deal in Company Securities (including hedging arrangements) at any time without the Chairman's prior consent, and must notify the Company Secretary of intention to trade and confirm afterwards.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Must not deal in Company Securities without the prior approval of the Board or the next most senior director; must also notify and confirm trades to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Employees other than executives
tiers.description: May deal in Company Securities at any time (no consent required) provided the Company Secretary is notified before the transaction and confirmation is given afterwards, and the employee is not in possession of inside information; strongly advised (not required) to limit dealing to the recommended trading period.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in the Company Securities

windows.start_anchor: date of the Company's AGM, or release of its quarterly activities report, half yearly results, yearly results, or a prospectus/disclosure document offering equity securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: None described. The 4-week trading period is only 'recommended' guidance, not a mandatory closed period; there is no mechanism described for imposing an additional prohibition.

rules.detail: Company Securities expressly includes derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures and options. A director or executive must not deal in Company Securities without the Chairman's prior consent, and must notify and confirm the trade to the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures and options ... A director or executive ... must not deal in the Company Securities without the prior consent of the Chairman of the Board.

rules.detail: Employees may deal in an OTC derivative referencing Company shares at any time provided they notify the Company Secretary before commencing and confirm afterwards, and are not in possession of inside information; no consent required.
rules.evidence: Employees may deal in the Company Securities at any time provided the Employee notifies the Company Secretary before commencing the transaction and, after the transaction has occurred, provides confirmation of the trading.

rules.detail: The definition of 'deal' expressly includes entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in Company Securities; for a director or executive this requires the Chairman's prior consent like any other dealing. No vesting-state distinction is drawn.
rules.evidence: entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in the Company Securities.

rules.detail: The Chairman must not enter a hedging arrangement without prior approval of the Board or the next most senior director.
rules.evidence: The Chairman must not deal in Company Securities without the prior approval of the Board or the next most senior director.

rules.detail: Employees may enter a hedging arrangement at any time with notification and post-trade confirmation, provided they are not in possession of inside information.
rules.evidence: entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in the Company Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure would be an 'agreement to sell' or an arrangement limiting economic risk, both captured by the 'deal' definition, requiring the Chairman's prior consent for a director/executive.
rules.evidence: subscribing for, purchasing or selling the Company Securities or entering into an agreement to do any of those things.

rules.detail: For employees, a monetisation structure is a 'deal' requiring only notification before and confirmation after, provided the person holds no inside information.
rules.evidence: subscribing for, purchasing or selling the Company Securities or entering into an agreement to do any of those things.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not separately named but fall within 'other financial products' issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares; a director/executive needs the Chairman's prior consent to enter one.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures and options.

rules.detail: For employees, a CFD referencing Company shares only requires notification before and confirmation after dealing.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures and options.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not named or otherwise addressed anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not addressed anywhere.
Secured financing arrangements of any kind are not addressed anywhere in the policy.

Designated Persons should not engage in short term trading; purchase with a view to resale, or sale with a view to repurchase, within 12 months is treated as short-term. Selling shares immediately after acquiring them via conversion of a security (eg option exercise) is not short-term.
rules.evidence: In general, the purchase of Company Securities with a view to resale within a 12 month period and the sale of Company Securities with a view to repurchase within a 12 month period would be considered to be transactions of a "short term" nature.

exceptions.evidence: acquire the Company ordinary shares by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares.
acquire the Company Securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class.
acquire the Company Securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class.

acquire, or agree to acquire, options under a Company share option plan; and exercise options acquired under a Company share option plan (but may not sell all or part of the shares received upon exercise of the options other than in accordance with these procedures).

exemption_authority: None described. There is no closed period regime and no hardship or court-order exemption process. Directors and executives require the Chairman's prior consent to deal at any time (the Chairman requires Board or next-senior-director approval); no further exemption pathway is set out.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In this policy "Company Securities" includes ... derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, debentures and options.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC put/call written by a bank over UOS shares is expressly, not merely inferentially, a 'Company Security', so entering it is squarely a regulated dealing requiring the Chairman's consent for directors/executives.

bespoke_clauses.clause: To "deal" in the Company Securities includes ... entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings in the Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This clause is a direct description of a collar; it confirms the hedge is a 'deal' subject to the same consent/notification regime as an outright sale, with no separate vesting-based hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the recommended time (in terms of avoiding suggestions of insider trading) for any Designated Person to deal in the Company Securities is during the 4 week period from [AGM/quarterly/half-year/annual results/prospectus release].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no binding closed period; timing of collar entry, unwind or roll is governed mainly by Chairman consent and the absence of inside information, not by a hard blackout calendar, giving more scheduling flexibility.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to all directors, executives, employees, contractors, consultants and advisors ... of United Overseas Australia Limited.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing are never mentioned, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not directly regulated by this document; the bank should confirm the Company Secretary's view before relying on this silence.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no lender forced-sale or takeover carve-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: (no equivalent clause found in the policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many ASX peers, there is no express exception for a secured lender's forced sale on default, or for dealing under a takeover/scheme of arrangement, so enforcement of the loan against the collateral shares would still require the Chairman's consent (or, for an employee, notification) even on default.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Please find attached a copy of the "Securities Dealing Policy" ... (letter addressed to both the Australian Securities Exchange and the Singapore Stock Exchange).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company also reports to the Singapore Stock Exchange and has a Malaysian office; this policy text does not reference SGX-specific dealing restrictions, so the bank should independently confirm whether additional overlay requirements apply.

summary: UOS's policy expressly defines 'Company Securities' to include derivatives and other financial products issued by third parties in relation to the Company's shares, and its definition of 'deal' expressly includes entering into agreements or transactions which operate to limit the economic risk of a person's holdings, so an OTC put/call collar with a bank is squarely and expressly a regulated dealing rather than one caught only by inference. Directors and executives may not deal (including hedge) at all without the Chairman's prior consent (the Chairman needs Board or next-senior-director approval), and must notify and later confirm the trade to the Company Secretary; there is no binding closed period, only a non-mandatory 4-week 'recommended' trading window tied to results, AGM and prospectus releases, so timing is governed mainly by consent and the absence of inside information. The policy is silent on margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing, so the loan leg of a funded collar is not directly addressed, has no express prohibition or exemption process, and (unusually) has no carve-out for a secured lender's forced sale on default. A funded collar therefore appears structurally available for directors/executives subject to the Chairman's consent for both the derivative legs and any settlement dealing, provided the arrangement is not short-term (a purchase/resale or sale/repurchase within 12 months, materially longer than the typical 3-month peer standard) and the person holds no inside information at the time.
